business: Nota (@NotaGetBot): a Telegram bot that collects receipts, invoices and handwritten delivery notes from work chats into the owner's Google Sheet and flags duplicates and arithmetic errors
by_segment: Remote investor in villas or a build, living abroad
Villa management company or villa rental operator
why_not: I would let it run on the free 30, but a café goes through 30 receipts in a week or two, and that is too short to know if my staff will keep sending properly or my admin will just go back to her Excel. I don't start a monthly bill for something we might drop after two weeks.
My bookkeeper already runs everything through Zoho Expense and it works well enough. I'm not moving my site receipts into a Google Sheet run by a Telegram bot just to skip a bit of typing.

I'd throw the free 30 receipts at it out of curiosity, but I wouldn't pay yet. Where I actually lost money was mechanics and staff padding cash receipts and handwritten notes, and a bot that types up a fake number neatly doesn't catch that. I'd still be checking every receipt myself.

I'd probably forward it a few receipts on the free 30 to see what happens, but I'm not putting a bot from a company I've never heard of into my work groups and paying monthly for it in the first month. I only look at the receipts when something smells wrong, so nothing forces me to switch this week.

I'd let it chew through the free 30 because it costs me nothing, but I'm not paying until I see it read our handwritten notas and faded shop receipts without me fixing every row. If I'm still correcting amounts in the group chat at midnight, I'm back where I started.

Most of what my guys send is a handwritten nota from the material shop, faded and half in shorthand, and I don't believe a bot reads those right. If I still have to check every row against the photo, I can wire up n8n and ChatGPT to a sheet myself over a weekend and not pay monthly for it.

I'd let it read the groups for free, sure, but with receipts landing every day in three or four chats those 30 documents are gone in about a week, before I know if anyone opens the sheet. After that my volume means the $35 plan, and that's another monthly bill I'd have to justify for something I'm not sure we'd keep up with.

I'd use the 30 free documents to see how it handles the messy receipts from the workshop, then wire up n8n and ChatGPT to my own sheet over a weekend. Paying $19 every month forever for something I can build myself doesn't make sense on my margins.

I pay the contractors myself by bank transfer, so my bank statement already is my expense list. I might forward a few screenshots to try the free 30, but I would not pay $19 a month for a sheet of payments I already made and can see.
why_yes: Flagging duplicates and wrong totals is exactly what I sit and check by hand since I caught someone double-claiming, and the free 30 with no card costs me nothing to test. If it reads my staff's handwritten nota correctly I'll pay the $35 without thinking, because that's nothing next to one inflated receipt.

I'm on the other side of the world scrolling the group chat at midnight trying to guess what got spent on the build, and my admin's sheet is always a week behind. The first 30 are free with no card, so I'll throw the bot in the group, and if the numbers hold up, $35 a month is nothing next to what a build leaks when nobody's watching.
flip: If the free 30 come back right on our worst handwritten notas and blurry photos, with no fixing from me, I'd pay without thinking about it.
A full free month, so I can see one whole month of the café in the sheet with my admin not typing anything, before I put in a card.
If it caught the receipts my site manager pays in cash that never show up in my bank, and compared them against the build budget so I could see overspend before I send the next transfer.
Running my own pile of real handwritten nota through the free 30 and seeing almost all of them come out right with no fixing. If it handles those better than what I could hack together, $19 is fine.
If it pushed the receipts straight into Zoho or Jurnal instead of a separate sheet, so my bookkeeper keeps her setup and I only use it to grab receipts from the Telegram groups.
If during the free 30 it actually flags a duplicate or a padded total from my scooter repairs that I missed myself, I'd pay the $19 straight away.
Another villa operator in Bali I know telling me they've used it for months and it caught a duplicate or a padded receipt for them.
If I could just forward receipts to it myself without adding it to any group or connecting my Google account, and get the sheet back as a file, I would try the free 30.
If my admin ran the free 30 documents on a messy week of fuel and parts receipts and told me it saved her most of a day without errors, I'd pay.
Seeing it on my own receipts during the free 30: a scribbled mechanic note and a fuel slip turned into correct rows in my sheet, plus proof it caught a duplicate or a wrong total my admin missed.
Another contractor here in Bali I know telling me they've run it on their site chats for a few months with no problems, plus a real company name and a clear statement of what it stores and deletes.
My bookkeeper telling me she already uses it with her other clients and wants me on it, or another contractor I know who has run it for six months or more.
A full first month free covering all our groups instead of 30 documents, so I can see if we really use the sheet and the Monday report before I pay anything.

If it worked without touching my Google account or the group (my admin forwards the receipts and gets back a sheet or file she uploads herself), plus a real company name and a written policy on where the documents are stored and when they get deleted.
If it pushed the rows straight into Jurnal so my bookkeeper stops retyping, and on the free trial it actually flagged a double-sent receipt from my own staff.
If it reads handwritten Indonesian notes and blurry transfer screenshots clearly better than my own ChatGPT setup does, and the sheet and folder stay fully mine and keep working if Nota shuts down.
